scope: Read actual prototype, saved report, corrected assessment and overlap hashes. Independently derived boundary and averaged momentum identities. No new numerical/model run or scientific source edits.
findings: Material coordinates x=X and y=a cos(kX-omega t) prescribe an anchored extensible sheet with zero horizontal material velocity. This removes the separate inextensibility/swimming-force ambiguity.

Taking the periodic stationary limit before the far-field limit selects bounded mean pumping without imposing a counterflow at infinity. Zero mean pressure gradient and zero distant shear close the mean equation; the amplitude coefficient is then defined at fixed finite frequency, wave number and viscosity.

For exp[i(kx-omega t)], the decaying branch s=sqrt(k^2-i omega/nu), psi(0)=omega/k and psi_prime(0)=0 give the stated first-order velocity. Expanding no-slip at the material boundary gives U(0)/a^2=-Re(psi_second(0))/2=omega Re(s)/2 with the correct sign.

Period-averaged incompressible NS gives nu U_second=partial_y mean(u1 v1). Since mean(u1 v1) and U_prime vanish far away, nu U_prime=mean(u1 v1). The resulting integral correction and prototype complex-conjugation convention are correct.

The source is a completed unsteady-Stokes/moving-boundary approximation: correct linear inertia and geometric pumping but no convective transport in the mean equation. Convection and the requested pumping both first occur at quadratic amplitude, so dropping it is a physical closure error at the observable order.

The reference independently solves the fourth-order linear vorticity boundary ODE and then the mean-momentum BVP with direct averaged convective acceleration. It does not insert the analytic modal integral. Finite-depth and tolerance refinements are reported.

Oscillatory velocity decays in the far field, so the measured far-field pumping requires no additional particle-following/Stokes-drift correction. Ordinary positive signals and zero-frequency Taylor limits are consistent.
